title: Group Fitness Class Passes: how a corporate wellness enrollment reduces the no-show fee
content:
## Scope
This document covers the Group Fitness Class Passes product line. It states how the flat no-show fee charged when a booked class is missed is affected by the member also holding an active corporate wellness enrollment.

## Basis
A member who holds an active corporate wellness enrollment at the time a no-show is logged has the tier's flat no-show fee reduced. The reduction rate applied is the lesser of two rates: the employer's own discount rate under that corporate wellness enrollment, and this tier's own corporate wellness discount rate. Whichever of the two is lower is the rate actually applied to reduce the fee; the two rates are never added together and never applied one after the other. A member who does not hold an active corporate wellness enrollment at that time is charged the tier's full flat no-show fee, with no reduction. The fee charged, whether reduced or full, is rounded to two decimal places.

## Condition table
| Holds active corporate wellness enrollment at the time logged? | Fee charged |
|---|---|
| No | The tier's full flat no-show fee |
| Yes | The full fee reduced by the lesser of the employer's discount rate and the tier's own corporate wellness discount rate |

## Hypothetical worked example (illustration only)
Suppose, purely for illustration, a tier's flat no-show fee were $20.00, the tier's own corporate wellness discount rate were 8 percent, and an enrolled member's employer offered a 5 percent rate under its enrollment. Because 5 percent is the lesser of the two rates, the fee actually charged is $20.00 reduced by 5 percent, rounded to two decimal places. Had the employer's rate instead been 12 percent, the lesser rate would be the tier's own 8 percent, and that is the rate that would apply instead.

## Points of judgement
- Whether the enrollment is active is judged at the moment the no-show is logged, not at the moment the class was originally booked or missed.
- Only one rate is ever applied to the full fee — never the sum of the two rates, and never a second reduction layered on top of the first.
